description:
Extend the builtin pattern of clz/ctz/popcount/mulhi (defk-52v.6): a builtin with a precise integer definition, a portable C fallback, a hardware instruction where one exists, and an Elixir-mode implementation with agreement properties.

- Start with crc32c(acc, word) for u8/u32/u64 words (ARMv8 CRC32C*, SSE4.2 crc32). Measure examples/hashes.exs CRC32C against crc32cer (today crc32cer is 14x faster than the kernel).
- Then, if the research ticket supports it: carry-less multiply (CRC32/CRC64 folding, GHASH), and possibly single AES/SHA rounds; compare with :crypto.
- Decide how a builtin picks its implementation in a portable build: only the fallback; runtime dispatch per call site (target_clones / a cached CPU-feature check); or only in an architecture build. Measure the dispatch cost.
- Devex: how the docs and errors present a builtin that is fast on one target and slow on another (docs/language.md Builtins table).

Done when crc32c is prototyped with all three implementations, agreement properties pass in both modes and under forced yields, and the speedup per target is recorded.
title: Prototype: hardware-instruction builtins with exact meanings (crc32c first)
